claims.implementation: backend/arkali/control/capability/capability_graph.py - CapabilityGraph.can_perform is the deterministic answer to "Can I perform this?". Pre-activation it returns NOT_CONFIGURED unchanged from Phase 3. Activated, it composes three inputs into one verdict: every external *_ref resolved at query time through resolve_references, the node's own configured_state, and its graph-owned prerequisites walked transitively by _refusal. PASS requires all of them; every other case is NOT_CONFIGURED. An unknown capability id and a prerequisite cycle RAISE rather than being answered, so a typo and a malformed graph cannot masquerade as a governed configuration state. backend/arkali/control/capability/activated_query.py - refusal_for decides one node's own inputs and documents why the negative state is NOT_CONFIGURED rather than FAIL or UNSUPPORTED: EXECUTION_AND_CAPABILITY.md §4 pairs `resolving` with `not being NOT_CONFIGURED`, FAIL is assigned to no capability query by the canonical set and would be misread as success by the unchanged accepted Phase 8 predicate `state is not NOT_CONFIGURED`, and UNSUPPORTED is canonically another context's verdict. The mapping is derived, not chosen. backend/arkali/control/capability/reference_resolution.py - ReferenceResolvers.resolve visits the canonical schema's fields in declaration order and each field's references in the order the node declares them, which is what makes the reason string as deterministic as the state. Nothing is cached at any layer: ReferenceResolvers holds the authorities and never their answers, and CapabilityGraph stores no verdict, so every query re-asks every authority.

Executed by the recorded runs in phase_9B_report.json.

claims.implementation: backend/arkali/control/capability/capability_node.py - the C-13 node carries provider_refs, permission_refs and evidence_requirement_refs and NOTHING else about those authorities. There is no health, availability, cost or fallback_configuration field, and extra="forbid" means one cannot be attached, so a shadow registry is prevented structurally rather than policed. validate_no_shadow_registry closes the one free-form escape hatch (runtime_requirements) and takes the provider-owned field names as an argument, because AUTHORITY_MAP.yaml provider_authority.fields_owned is their sole store (F-0013). backend/arkali/control/capability/reference_resolution.py - the ReferenceResolver Protocol declares exactly one method returning bool. A resolver cannot hand back a value, so a caller cannot store one: reference in, outcome out, never a value. ReferenceResolution records the field, the identifier, the owning authority, a state and a reason - no field on it can hold a referenced value either. backend/arkali/control/capability/reference_authority.py - the reference-to-authority binding is parsed from the canonical capability_node: block at call time and appears in no module as a literal, so a renamed authority renames itself here rather than expiring. It fails closed on an absent block, a block with no external reference, a block with no graph-internal reference, or an authority the map does not declare.

claims.implementation: backend/arkali/control/capability/capability_graph.py - the split ADR-0003 declares is realised as a derived phase fact, not a flag. is_activated compares activation_phase with current_phase, both supplied by the caller from authoritative state; the class judges neither and stores no activation boolean. activate() ALWAYS raises PrematureActivation, at the activation phase as well as before it, because a caller able to activate the graph would be deciding a governed fact locally. The activation phase itself is never written in the module: ARK-REQ-0048 carries it in the requirement register's Phase column and it is injected at construction, so hard-coding "9B" would put a governed value in a second place (F-0013). Pre-activation the query returns NOT_CONFIGURED with the ADR-0003 source, and at the activation phase with no authority composed it still returns NOT_CONFIGURED rather than inventing a verdict. Package 3 changed no module under backend/arkali/; the schema/activation split it claims is the one Packages 1 and 2 built and Phase 3 established.
